narrative.overview:
The dial is the knob's well of light seen from above, as in the logo. The hub at the centre is the light source and everything is lit from the centre outward: a dark ground that falls from a bluish centre to a near-black rim, white ink, and seat hues that exist only as light (a tint on the seat's glass, a soft halo behind its numeral, the colour of its label). A pending change is light gathering: an arc of white light runs once around the ring in exactly 800 ms, and when it closes the change is committed. The active player's zone is outlined: a thin line of that seat's hue along the three sides of its zone. This is the Lumineux theme, the default (`UI_THEME_DEFAULT`).

Two themes share one layout and one set of gestures. Booster, the wrapper theme shipped first, is kept as theme 2: saturated seat fields on wrapper black, a silver foil that seals a pending change, straight 2 px rules, no light. Each canonical section below describes Lumineux first, then what Booster does differently under "Theme 2: Booster". A rule stated for one theme binds that theme only; rules marked shared bind both. `ui_set_theme(theme, ground)` switches at run time and the firmware reads both values at start; the settings screen that lets the user choose is not built yet.

Density is low and the type is loud. Every screen has one huge condensed numeral or title, one line of uppercase labels, and nothing else. Everything is drawn in code (LVGL 9.2 draw calls into one full-screen object on a 360×360 round LCD), and every layout is centred on (180, 180). The light is baked: the ground, the halos, the ring, the ray and the icons are alpha masks tinted at draw time, and no blur is computed per frame.

Rejected by the direction contract: flat colour quadrants, a thin progress ring on black, and the neon gamer HUD (scanlines, chrome bevels, hexagon grids). Rejected by the user (2026-11-12): any zigzag or crimped edge. The product record takes the spirit of a third-party dial app without copying its colours, icons, logo or composition. Wizards of the Coast materials are allowed by the owner (PRODUCT.md, Brand Commitments).
keyCharacteristics: Two themes, one layout, one set of gestures. Lumineux is the default; Booster is theme 2.
Lumineux: a radial dark ground, white ink, and seat hues used as light on glass, never as paint.
The hub is the light source: turn marker, pending value and undo all live there, and the active seat's zone is outlined in its hue.
Pending is always an arc or band whose drawn extent is the elapsed share of the 800 ms commit delay.
Condensed ExtraBold numerals and SemiBold uppercase labels, kerning off, in both themes.
A seat is never identified by hue alone: every seat carries its J1–J4 label and its position.
Every arena seat faces its player.
All light is pre-computed alpha masks; nothing is blurred at run time.

rules.name: The Hue Is Light Rule
rules.body: In Lumineux a seat hue is never an opaque field. It is a translucent tint on glass, a halo, or the colour of a label. Numerals and chrome stay in Light Ink.

rules.name: The Seat Owns Its Hue Rule
rules.body: Shared. Seat hues mark seats only. Chrome (buttons, menu focus, focus marks, the undo pill, the pending arc, the rays) is never drawn in a seat hue; in Lumineux focus is white light.

rules.name: The Dark Ground Rule
rules.body: Every ground preset keeps Light Ink at 7:1 or more on the bare ground; `host/shots.c` asserts it for all six (computed: 12.0 to 17.0 at the centre, 18 or more at the rim). The rim is 27 % of each channel of the centre, rounded, which maps the Nuit centre exactly onto Well Rim. A new preset must pass the same assertion.

rules.name: The Low Light Under Numerals Rule
rules.body: Light behind a white numeral is kept low so the numeral stays readable: Solo halo at 40 %, the selected seat's glass at 46/255 (36/255 unselected), its halo at 20 %, the sheet and game-over halos at 30 %. The target is 7:1 for numerals and 4.5:1 for text on glass. Do not raise these values to make a seat look brighter.

rules.name: The One Foil Rule
rules.body: Booster only. The foil is Booster's only gradient and it shows only while a delta is pending.

rules.name: The No Fade Rule
rules.body: Booster only. Everything is drawn at full opacity. Defeat is shown by dropping the field fill and replacing the total with the skull mark in full seat hue, never by lowering alpha. (Lumineux does the opposite on purpose: a defeated seat goes dark.)

rules.name: The Real Minus Rule
rules.body: Shared. Negative deltas use U+2212 (−), not a hyphen. Positive deltas always show "+".

rules.name: The All Caps Rule
rules.body: Shared. Every label and row is uppercase French, taken from `ui/strings_fr.h`. Beyond letters and numerals, text carries only signed deltas and the separators "·", "=", "/", "›" and "—" (a rule that is off).

rules.name: The Drawn Pointer Rule
rules.body: Shared. In text rows (journal, menu, undo) a hand-off or attack is written with U+203A as the separator ("J3 › J1"). In the pending hub the pointer is a drawn filled triangle between the two J#, never a glyph. The +/− beside a selected total are drawn 2 px marks (18 px), never glyphs.

rules.name: The Seats Face Their Players Rule
rules.body: Shared. An arena seat's numeral, label, +/− marks and tap zones all live in that seat's frame, turned by (seat angle − 90°), with the label on the rim side. Never lay out a seat element in screen coordinates.

rules.name: The Parted By Ground Rule
rules.body: Lumineux only. Seats are separated by a wedge of ground (2° trimmed from each side of each sector, in whole degrees), never by a drawn line.

rules.name: The Baked Light Rule
rules.body: No blur, glow or radial gradient is computed per frame. Light is an alpha mask blit: pre-rendered by `ui/assets/glow_gen.py`, or computed once and cached (halos per radius, the well per ground). A new light effect must fit that model.

rules.name: The Never Light Alone Rule
rules.body: A halo, a tint or a ray never carries information alone. The seat is named by its J# and its position, the active seat by the hub's J#, defeat by the skull and the word VAINCU. If a halo cannot be allocated it is simply not drawn and nothing is lost.

rules.name: The Rule Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: Booster only. Separate planes with a straight seam in the rule weight, never with a shadow, a glow or an offset.

rules.name: The No Zigzag Rule
rules.body: Shared. The user rejected the jagged look (2026-11-12). No zigzag, toothed, serrated or crimped edge on any line, seam, ring, band or arc. Every pending indicator is a smooth form whose drawn extent is the progress.

rules.name: The One Rule Weight Rule
rules.body: Booster only. 2 px everywhere, with one exception, the 6 px active-seat crest.

rules.name: The Hub-Only Repaint Rule
rules.body: Shared. Arena seats show committed values. While only the pending value, the arc or the undo state changes, invalidate the hub box and never the turned seat layers. The box is the hub radius plus 18 px in Lumineux (the glow passes the edge) and plus 6 px in Booster.

dos: Do treat Lumineux as the default. Design a new screen in Lumineux first, then give Booster the same layout and tap zones.
Do keep numerals in ink in Lumineux, and show the seat hue as glass tint, halo and label.
Do show pending state as an arc (Lumineux) or a foil seal (Booster) whose drawn extent equals the elapsed share of the commit delay (800 ms, linear), with nothing drawn ahead of it.
Do pair every seat hue with its J1–J4 label and its position.
Do mark the thing to tap with white light: a lit pill border, a white halo, the hub's glow.
Do keep light behind numerals at the shipped levels (Solo halo 40 %, selected glass 46/255, seat halo 20 %, sheet and game-over halos 30 %).
Do build every light effect from an A8 mask that is pre-rendered or cached, and give every new raster a provenance line in `ui/assets/README.md`.
Do take every user-facing string from `ui/strings_fr.h`, in uppercase.
Do draw each arena seat in its own frame, turned by (seat angle − 90°), with the label on the rim side.
Do keep the hub the single place for turn, undo and pending state, and repaint only the hub while only it changes.
Do check a new ground preset with the 7:1 assertion in `host/shots.c`.
donts: Don't paint an opaque seat field in Lumineux, and don't add halos, glass or rays to Booster.
Don't use a seat hue for chrome, focus, the pending arc, the undo or the rays.
Don't compute a blur, a glow or a radial gradient per frame.
Don't let a halo, a tint or a ray be the only signal of anything.
Don't draw rules between Lumineux seats; they are parted by ground.
Don't draw a zigzag, toothed or crimped edge anywhere; the user rejected it.
Don't use a hyphen for minus, or a glyph for the hub pointer, the +/− marks, the skull or an icon.
Don't fade a defeated seat in Booster, and don't leave a defeated seat lit in Lumineux.
Don't fall back to the category default (flat colour quadrants, a thin progress ring on black) or to a neon gamer HUD (scanlines, chrome bevels, hexagon grids).
Don't copy the third-party dial app's colours, icons, logo or composition.
